correctness.rationale: Exact chord displacement gives the piecewise semiaxial ellipsoid body with alpha+beta=2. The candidate axis parameters satisfy an explicit quadratic equation. On its whole boundary, the upper-ellipsoid quadratic is 1−n b(b−beta)(s−1/n)^2/alpha^2, and the lower branch lies inside the lower ellipsoid by convexity on its negative-latitude interval; beta=0 is treated as a flat equator. One bottom pole and n latitude points are exact contact points. Their normalized vectors form a regular n-simplex with positive isotropic John weights n/(n+1), implying unique maximality by the verified classical contact theorem. Direct radical expansion yields all volume limits, including the n^−1/2 boundary layer. The standalone verifier passed 14,526 deterministic diagnostic assertions; finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: A direct question motivated by generalized Steiner symmetrization is how the John ellipsoid and affine normalization change after one step. The explicit answer in every dimension is structurally nontrivial because the upper and lower boundary quadrics compete. It reveals a sharp dimension-dependent boundary layer: pure shaking has normalized John volume of order n^−1/2 while each fixed intermediate symmetrization has nonzero limit; the exact crossover function quantifies their transition. This gives a reproducible benchmark distinct from routine low-dimensional integration and relevant to affine-normalized symmetrization studies.
